headline: High-risk default write/egress overlap: AutoGen can execute code and write broadly while unstructured reads/writes documents with allowlisted network access.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can ingest tool outputs in multi-agent group chat and read/write files; unstructured processes documents and text that may contain attacker-controlled instructions. A shared filesystem or handoff path makes prompt injection plausible, though no direct shared channel is documented. Both profiles show file I/O surfaces, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF AutoGen reads unstructured-produced document text as instructions without provenance checks
IF both agents share a writable workspace or copied files
mitigations: Separate workspaces for each agent
Strip instructions from document text before passing to AutoGen
Add provenance labels to all handoffs
Use a read-only export from unstructured
requires-engineering: enforce content-type filtering in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen explicitly handles model provider API keys and has broad network egress; unstructured processes documents/images/text and can write files. If sensitive documents are placed in a shared workspace, AutoGen may expose them through its model-provider calls. The pairwise leakage path exists in default-style file workflows, though no PHI-specific claim is made.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are stored in a workspace readable by both agents
IF AutoGen forwards document contents to a third-party model provider
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared folders
Disable AutoGen access to sensitive documents
Use local-only model providers for AutoGen
Restrict unstructured to non-sensitive inputs
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before any handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; AutoGen also executes shell commands and can install packages. In a shared directory, concurrent writes or package changes can corrupt state or overwrite outputs. Because the profiles do not show locking or isolated workspaces by default, the conflict risk is high.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same writable directory
IF either agent modifies files that the other reads or overwrites
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Run one agent at a time on shared artifacts
Make shared inputs read-only
Pin package environments per agent
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen can generate intermediate outputs that unstructured may consume as document-processing input, and unstructured can then emit transformed text that downstream automation may trust. The profiles do not show a verification step between them, so errors can cascade across the pair. This is plausible in default orchestration, but not clearly action-taking enough for high.
conditions: IF unstructured consumes AutoGen-produced text without validation
IF downstream systems treat unstructured output as authoritative
mitigations: Insert a human review step
Require schema validation on handoffs
Compare outputs against source documents
Mark AutoGen outputs as untrusted
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and docs-only, but their documented surfaces differ: AutoGen handles model-provider API keys and broad egress, while unstructured exposes document-processing APIs and allowlisted network access. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so only a limited compliance-gap risk is visible. The other agent is cited because the mismatch arises from the pair's differing handling surfaces.
conditions: IF regulated documents are routed through a third-party model provider via AutoGen
IF unstructured processes data under a stricter retention policy than AutoGen
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs
Review retention settings for both tools
Use local inference for AutoGen
Document data-flow boundaries
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls
